CNN agreed, and thus was born `Smerconish', an hourlong Saturday morning program that takes after its host's independent views. Using a topical, conversational format, he aims for the TV show to be an extension of his weekday radio broadcast, with free-flowing topics and the ability to discuss issues that strike a chord with the audience. Along the same lines, he thinks it's important to present the content in an engaging manner, free of my-way-or-the-highway ideology. Smerconish, who has a law degree from the University of Pennsylvania, is also a New York Times' best-selling author.
programme.title: Smerconish

programme.desc: S3 E4 — Burnley v Blackburn Rovers Burnley v Blackburn Rovers (Kick-off 12.00pm). Hugh Woozencroft presents coverage of the Championship match from Turf Moor, as the rivals face each other in the East Lancashire derby. There have been 170 previous meetings between these teams in all competitions, dating back to the 1888/89 season, and it is the Clarets who narrowly hold the better record with 71 wins to Rovers 65, with the other 34 games ending in draws. The most recent meeting was in the 2024/25 campaign and saw Burnley triumph 1-0 at Ewood Park, with the corresponding clash here ending in a 1-1 stalemate. With analysis from Ben Mee and Brad Friedel, commentary by Seb Hutchinson and Lucy Ward, and reports from Katie Shanahan.
programme.title: EFL Live

programme.desc: Burnley v Blackburn Rovers Burnley take on Blackburn Rovers in the East Lancashire Derby, and there is famous and old rivalry between the two clubs. Just 11 miles separates the two towns, and the first time they played each was in 1884, and they have met many times since. Burnley were relegated from the Premier League last season, and have struggled so far in the second tier they parted company with their manager Nicky Hayen last month, and Fabio Celestini is now in charge.

programme.desc: S3 E4 — Burnley v Blackburn Rovers Burnley v Blackburn Rovers (Kick-off 12.00pm). Hugh Woozencroft presents coverage of the Championship match from Turf Moor, as the rivals face each other in the East Lancashire derby. There have been 170 previous meetings between these teams in all competitions, dating back to the 1888/89 season, and it is the Clarets who narrowly hold the better record with 71 wins to Rovers 65, with the other 34 games ending in draws. The most recent meeting was in the 2024/25 campaign and saw Burnley triumph 1-0 at Ewood Park, with the corresponding clash here ending in a 1-1 stalemate. With analysis from Ben Mee and Brad Friedel, commentary by Seb Hutchinson and Lucy Ward, and reports from Katie Shanahan.
programme.title: EFL Live

programme.desc: Burnley v Blackburn Rovers Burnley take on Blackburn Rovers in the East Lancashire Derby, and there is famous and old rivalry between the two clubs. Just 11 miles separates the two towns, and the first time they played each was in 1884, and they have met many times since. Burnley were relegated from the Premier League last season, and have struggled so far in the second tier they parted company with their manager Nicky Hayen last month, and Fabio Celestini is now in charge.

programme.desc: S3 E4 — Burnley v Blackburn Rovers Burnley v Blackburn Rovers (Kick-off 12.00pm). Hugh Woozencroft presents coverage of the Championship match from Turf Moor, as the rivals face each other in the East Lancashire derby. There have been 170 previous meetings between these teams in all competitions, dating back to the 1888/89 season, and it is the Clarets who narrowly hold the better record with 71 wins to Rovers 65, with the other 34 games ending in draws. The most recent meeting was in the 2024/25 campaign and saw Burnley triumph 1-0 at Ewood Park, with the corresponding clash here ending in a 1-1 stalemate. With analysis from Ben Mee and Brad Friedel, commentary by Seb Hutchinson and Lucy Ward, and reports from Katie Shanahan.
programme.title: EFL Live

"I want people to say that our show is smart. I want our show to be authentic", Burnett says in a promo. "I want our show to have courage". Left unsaid, of course, is that she wants her show to have a big audience, too.

programme.desc: S1 — Midlands - A Celestial Projector is Brought Back to Life The team help a charity get their iconic bus back on the road, Mark Stuckey reaches for the stars fixing an unusual projector, and Will is wowed by the lost art of encaustic tiles.
programme.title: The Repair Shop: On the Road

programme.desc: S1 — Midlands - A Celestial Projector Is Brought Back to Life Dominic Chinea and Mark Stuckey are in the Black Country, tackling the needs of a big red bus. After being used as a mobile shelter by a homelessness charity for a few years, a leaking roof and outdated electrics have combined to keep it off the road. It's a huge fix to take on, in every sense, and the team needs all the help vintage vehicle restorer Mark Owen can provide if they're to get it back into service. Plus, Pauline presents a celestial projector, once owned by her husband. Now the light has stopped working, and many of the constellations have worn away.
programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
